headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and data leakage; ms-swift’s file-reading/writing plus AutoGPT’s filesystem and shell access create unsafe default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and ms-swift can read/write files and emit logs/configs/training outputs. That creates a plausible shared-file pathway where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be interpreted as instructions by the other. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF ms-swift writes prompt-like text into logs, configs, or outputs that AutoGPT later reads
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable AutoGPT access to ms-swift output folders
Prefix shared files with machine-readable schemas only
Review any file AutoGPT ingests before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; ms-swift reads and writes datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files and handles hub/sdk tokens. If they share a workspace, sensitive training artifacts or secrets can flow from ms-swift into AutoGPT outputs or outbound requests. The pair is open-source, but the shared-file leakage path is credible in default-like setups.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF ms-swift stores tokens, checkpoints, or logs in paths AutoGPT can read
IF AutoGPT is allowed to send retrieved file contents over its allowlisted network egress
mitigations: Place secrets and checkpoints outside AutoGPT-readable paths
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token before co-running
Restrict AutoGPT egress to non-sensitive endpoints
Run each agent under separate OS users
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, and AutoGPT can spawn subprocesses while ms-swift can install packages and write files. Even though ms-swift does not modify git state, overlapping write and execution capabilities on a shared directory can race on files, configs, or installed dependencies. The conflict is real but narrower than a full git-state collision.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory
IF ms-swift installs or rewrites packages while AutoGPT is running subprocesses
IF either agent writes to files the other reads without locking
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments
Assign distinct working directories
Pause one agent during package installation by the other
Avoid shared mutable config files
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate plans or file-based outputs, and ms-swift exposes CLI/Python workflows that may consume those outputs as inputs. If ms-swift treats AutoGPT-produced artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into training, evaluation, or configuration changes. There is no documented verification barrier in either profile, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF ms-swift consumes AutoGPT-generated files, configs, or prompts without validation
IF AutoGPT output is used to drive training, evaluation, or deployment commands
mitigations: Require human review of AutoGPT outputs before reuse
Validate schemas for any exchanged files
Keep AutoGPT outputs read-only to ms-swift
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift explicitly touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and network egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches through file reuse and outbound transmission. The profiles do not state HIPAA/GDPR specifics, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ms-swift datasets, checkpoints, or logs
IF AutoGPT is permitted to read and transmit those files
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Document retention rules for logs and checkpoints
Disable outbound access for sensitive runs
Separate environments by data classification
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
